general.summary: The AI debt binge is the most recent example that underwriting standards have deteriorated in credit markets, with lenders increasingly fueling businesses that are “much less creditworthy” than in the past, according to Polus Capital Management’s Robert Dafforn.

general.title: Once the Regional Laggard in Sustainable Debt, Mexico Now Leads
general.summary: Mexico’s government has issued a record amount of sustainable debt this year, bucking a decline in such sales seen across emerging-markets as local pension funds step up investments.

general.title: Helsing Pulls Back From Plymouth UK Project After Losing Out on Navy Contract
general.summary: Helsing, Europe’s most valuable defense startup, is retreating from its flagship project in the UK to manufacture underwater naval drones a year after unveiling the plan with political fanfare, according to people familiar with the matter.

general.title: Southeast Asia’s data center boom leaned on Chinese demand. New U.S. rules put that pipeline at risk
general.summary: The rules require data centers in Southeast Asia to seek U.S. approval to buy advanced AI chips, threatening to slow a build-out fueled heavily on Chinese demand.

general.title: Anthropic Said to Guide IPO Pricing Above Market Range
general.summary: Anthropic is guiding prospective investors in its initial public offering that it expects to price the shares above the range, according to a person familiar with the matter. The AI model maker is on the cusp of pricing potentially the biggest IPO of all time. Ed Ludlow reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Anthropic likely to price IPO above the current range of $70 to $78, sources tell CNBC
general.summary: Anthropic is slated to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" and start trading on Nov. 19.

general.title: US Housing Starts Climb on Multifamily Construction Rebound
general.summary: US homebuilders started more homes in October, driven largely by a rebound in apartment construction while the single-family market remained challenged by high mortgage rates.

general.title: Ferguson CFO on AI Boom, Housing Pressure and $1.6 Billion Deal
general.summary: Ferguson CFO Bill Brundage discusses how higher rates and affordability are weighing on housing while AI, data centers and other large capital projects drive industrial demand. He also discusses inflation pressures and Ferguson’s $1.6 billion acquisition of FlowWorks. He spoke with Guy Johnson on Bloomberg Brief. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.title: Higher Rates Will Push Firms to Private Credit as Stress Rises
general.summary: Rising interest rates are set to impede access to public markets for more borrowers, prompting them to seek funds from private credit lenders instead.

general.title: Tencent Says US Chip Curbs to Slow Chinese AI in the Short Run
general.summary: Tencent Holdings Ltd. conceded that new Washington curbs on Chinese access to overseas data centers will hamper development of its next AI model, though the country will move increasingly toward domestic semiconductors to mitigate the longer-term impact.

general.title: Carlyle: We Don't Know the AI Model Yet as Credit Investors
general.summary: Mark Jenkins, co-president and head of global credit and insurance at Carlyle, says that as credit investors "we don’t really know what the model is yet for AI." He made the comments at Bloomberg's Global Credit Forum in London. (Source: Bloomberg)

general.summary: Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller said inflation remains headed in the wrong direction, urging the central bank to consider a larger, half-percentage-point rate hike at its December meeting.
